subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent dry-run mode, and what exact side-effect boundary must it guarantee across Gateway, embedded, plugin, client, and deferred tool execution paths?
rationale: The feature is useful and aligned with safer defaults, but the requested behavior defines a security-sensitive execution contract that automation should not invent from a single proposed implementation sketch.

options.title: Define the core contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify CLI scope, Gateway/embedded context propagation, plugin/client/deferred tool handling, and redaction before accepting an implementation.

options.title: Accept a narrow CLI-only experiment
options.body: Allow an explicitly limited `openclaw agent --dry-run` prototype if it documents uncovered surfaces and does not claim a universal safety guarantee.

options.title: Decline the global mode
options.body: Close the direction in favor of existing `tools.allow`/`tools.deny`, sandboxing, plugin hooks, and broader safe-workflow discussions.

recommendation.title: Define the core contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify CLI scope, Gateway/embedded context propagation, plugin/client/deferred tool handling, and redaction before accepting an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this account to agent tool adapter and runtime safety work, and the decision is about the product/security boundary rather than a narrow code defect.
